applicable_when: The kernel is L1/shared-memory bound (L1 at 92.85%, DRAM at only 12.86%). The dominant bottleneck is 8-way shared memory bank conflicts on the B-matrix loads inside the k-loop. The B matrix has stride_bn=480, stride_bk=1, meaning consecutive threads in the BLOCK_K dimension access the same bank (480 % 32 = 0 -> stride-32 conflict pattern). This causes 210M+ excessive wavefronts. Additionally, 168 registers/thread caps occupancy at 18.75%, leaving schedulers starved (only 0.68 eligible warps/cycle, 58.96% no-eligible cycles). Adding @triton.autotune will explore smaller BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N/BLOCK_K combinations that reduce register pressure, improve occupancy, and allow the compiler to generate better shared memory layouts. Increasing num_stages enables software pipelining to hide the remaining shared memory latency.
